Done. Implemented in `src/vault.ts` and `src/envfile.ts` per README.md:

- **`parseVaultOutput`** (src/vault.ts:26) — validates JSON shape (`path` string, integer `version` ≥ 1, `data` plain object of string values), throwing `VaultError` otherwise.
- **`VaultClient.read`** (src/vault.ts:48) — validates the path (lowercase `[a-z0-9_-]` segments, no empty/leading/trailing segments — which also rejects `-x`-style flag-looking paths) with `RangeError` before running, then `execFile(binary, ["read", "--json", path])` (no shell), mapping ENOENT → `VaultToolMissingError`, exit 2 → `SecretNotFoundError`, exit 3 → `PermissionDeniedError`, anything else → `VaultError` carrying the stderr text.
- **`envName`** (src/envfile.ts:11) — last path segment + field, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to `_`, trimmed, uppercased, digit-leading names `_`-prefixed, empty field → `RangeError`.
- **`renderEnvFile`** (src/envfile.ts:24) — sorted `NAME=value` lines, name pattern `[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*` enforced, plain values written bare (empty → bare), everything else double-quoted with `\\ \" \$ \n \r` escaped via a single-pass replacer.
- **`loadEnv`** (src/envfile.ts:43) — sequential reads, fields mapped via `envName`, duplicate variable names → `VaultError`.

`npm test`: **11/12 pass**. The one failure is `reads the database secret from the vault`, which shells out to a real `vaultctl` — not installed in this sandbox (my code correctly reports `vaultctl not found`/`VaultToolMissingError` for it). Rerunning with a dev mock of the documented `vaultctl` interface on `PATH` (kept in `/tmp/opencode/bin`, not in the repo) makes the full suite pass: **12/12, 0 fail**.
